# 0001: nvcc 12.5 rejects explicit-template-parameter lambdas in `Algorithm.hpp`

## Upstream

- Project: spearhed
- URL: <https://github.com/ComputationalRadiationPhysics/spearhed>
- Path: `packages/pmacc/libs/llamaLite/include/llamaLite/Algorithm.hpp`
- Base commit: `aa79f32653452bdaea55d9786c57d1ab10a37b81`
- File content also matches upstream `5fe1c79238c5` (last change to this file).
- Upstream issue: not filed yet. Report it at
  <https://github.com/ComputationalRadiationPhysics/spearhed/issues> with the
  reproduction below; this note is the downstream record.

## Symptom

CUDA compilation with nvcc 12.5 (`V12.5.82`) fails while parsing
`include/llamaLite/Algorithm.hpp`:

```text
Algorithm.hpp:87:97: error: expected identifier before '>' token
   87 | template<IsRecord R, typename CurrentPath, typename Selector, template<typename> typename VisitorTrait>
Algorithm.hpp:134:97: error: expected identifier before '>' token
```

The diagnostic points at the template parameter list, so the failure looks like
a template template parameter problem. It is not.

## Root cause

nvcc 12.5's front end misparses an explicit-template-parameter lambda
(`[&]<std::size_t I>()`) in the body of a function template when another member
function template is visible in the same translation unit. The selectors in the
same header (`SelectAll`, `Include`, `Exclude`) are member function templates,
and so are templates from headers included before `Algorithm.hpp`.

Minimal reproduction, rejected by nvcc 12.5 and accepted by nvcc 13.4:

```cpp
#include <cstddef>
template<typename T> concept C = true;
struct S { template<typename P> static constexpr bool a(P) { return true; } };
template<C R, typename P, typename Q, template<typename> typename V>
constexpr void g(auto&& view, auto&&... args)
{
    auto l = [&]<std::size_t I>() {};
    l.template operator()<0>();
}
```

Reordering the header does not fix it: a member function template in any
earlier header triggers the same parser state. Naming the inner parameter of the
template template parameter does not fix it either. Only removing the
explicit-template-parameter lambda does.

## Patch

`detail::for_each_index` invokes a generic visitor once per index with the index
passed as `std::integral_constant<std::size_t, I>`:

```cpp
template<typename Visitor, std::size_t... Is>
constexpr void for_each_index(Visitor&& visitor, std::index_sequence<Is...>)
{
    (visitor(std::integral_constant<std::size_t, Is>{}), ...);
}
```

`iterate_recursive` and `iterate_path_recursive` bind `I` from the
`integral_constant` argument and call the helper instead of the
explicit-template-parameter lambda. Iteration order, selection decisions,
visitor calls, and the compile-time unrolling are unchanged. The helper is a
`constexpr` function template, so it remains usable from device code under the
same rules as the surrounding functions.

## Verification

- nvcc 12.5.82: minimal reproduction and the patched header compile.
- nvcc 13.4.92: patched header compiles.
- g++ 13.3: patched header and the upstream `tests/unit/iterate/iterate.cpp`
  translation unit compile.
- graphFlow CPU, CUDA, HIP, and SYCL builds and the llamaLite iteration tests
  pass with the patch (see the graphFlow commit that added this note).

## Removal

Drop this patch when the vendored copy moves to an upstream commit that no
longer uses explicit-template-parameter lambdas in a function template, or when
the minimum supported nvcc is 12.6 or newer.
